Team — technical inputs below, pulled from the infra runbook and the August test artifacts. I kept language suitable for auditors; call out if you want more detail.

1) Architecture summary (short):
Redwood runs a control plane and a separately managed serving runtime. For production hosted API we operate an active-active deployment across two primary regions (us-east-1 and us-west-2) with cross-region health checks and smart routing. Traffic is routed by policy at the edge; when a region shows degraded health we shift new sessions automatically to the healthy region. Persistent telemetry and audit logs are replicated to an object store with cross-region replication.

2) RTO / RPO by workload (targets):
- Synchronous low-latency text generation endpoints: RTO target = 3 minutes for request routing & DNS/edge reroute; functional RTO to reach comparable latency P90 = 8-12 minutes (primarily warm-up for model caches). RPO target = near-zero for request logs and audit events (replicated within 30s), RPO = best-effort for in-flight partial responses (we mark these as lost and surface retry logic).
- Streaming/chat sessions with KV cache: RTO target = 5 minutes to re-establish routing; functional RTO to restore full cache-hit parity = 10-20 minutes depending on active session size. RPO = minutes for KV cache state (we continuously write checkpoints to replicated storage; last checkpoint typically within 60s).
- Batch/async embeddings ingestion: RTO target = 15 minutes; RPO = near-zero for persisted ingestion queues (replicated across regions).

3) Multi-region failover behavior and steps (automatic):
- Monitoring: edge probes, regional health monitors, and model-serving heartbeat metrics.
- Triggering: automatic routing switch when regional health falls below thresholds (configurable per-customer).
- Failover actions: 1) edge DNS and routing updates; 2) model serving processes in healthy region accept new traffic; 3) prefix/KV cache warm-up begins using prioritized checkpoint replay; 4) telemetry continues to replicate to central store.
- Fallback policy: we maintain a warm standby of model weights on GPUs in the secondary region (quantized formats), enabling faster warm-up for commonly used models. Customers can choose more aggressive warm standby (higher cost) for sub-1-minute recovery.

4) Tests & evidence:
- Last full simulated regional failover: 2026-08-23. Summary attached (failover-test-summary-2026-08-23.pdf) and a redacted runbook we provide to customers (redwood_dr_runbook.pdf).
- Test results: edge reroute executed in <30s, control-plane reconvergence <180s, P95 latency restored to within 1.2x baseline after 9 minutes for text gen endpoints. KV cache parity reached after ~12 minutes for the largest session profiles tested.

5) Caveats & guidance:
- Cold-cache penalties: very large context windows and sparsely accessed model variants may see longer warm-up times; recommend pre-warming for critical workloads.
- Data residency: customers using Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) may have different failover behaviors; respond accordingly in questionnaire if CapitalBank plans private deployment.

I attached the runbook and test summary that are safe to share with CapitalBank (redacted of internal IPs). Let me know if you want raw logs or a more detailed post-mortem to include.
